subject: literature
passage: When Mr. Oduya finally agreed to sell the bicycle, he spent an entire Saturday preparing it. He oiled the chain, trued the wheels, and polished the frame until the old green paint shone. The buyer, a student from the college, paid what was asked without arguing and wheeled it toward the gate. At the last moment Mr. Oduya called him back, unscrewed the small brass bell from the handlebar, and put it in his pocket. "You can buy another for a few coins," he said. "This one was a gift." Mr. Oduya's behavior suggests that he ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: suspected that the student would not take proper care of the bicycle.
choices.B: valued the bell for reasons that had nothing to do with its cost.
choices.C: had decided at the last moment not to sell the bicycle after all.
choices.D: regretted the price he had agreed to and wanted to keep something back.

explanation.why: Mr. Oduya says the bell is cheap to replace yet keeps it because it was a gift. He is attached to it for its personal meaning, not its price, which is why he hands over the carefully prepared bicycle but not the bell.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Nothing in the text shows distrust of the student, who pays without arguing and takes the bicycle.
explanation.B: Correct. Keeping an inexpensive bell because it was a gift shows that its value to him is sentimental.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The sale goes through; he takes back only the bell.
explanation.D: Incorrect. He prepared the bicycle with care and sold it for the asked price; the bell, he says, is worth only a few coins.
